cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet, is in the middle of a vision of a temple, and he's telling it himself. A man has been walking him all over it with a measuring rod, wall after wall after WALL, and friend, I stamp cookies for a living and even I'd have asked for a cookie break. Now the man brings Ezekiel back to the gate that faces east.

cards.question: Ezekiel is standing at the gate that faces east when he sees the glory of the God of Israel coming. Which direction is it coming from?

cards.text: His voice is like the roar of many waters, and the earth shines with His glory. Friend, the brightest thing in my old junk drawer was a birthday candle somebody used once.
Ezekiel says this vision is like the one he saw when God came to destroy the city, and like the visions he saw by the River Kebar.

cards.question: Standing before the glory of the God of Israel, Ezekiel falls ___.
With Ezekiel facedown, the glory of the LORD enters the temple through the gate facing east. True or false?

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up and brings him into the inner court. Me? I hop everywhere I go, base and all, and I STILL show up out of breath.

cards.question: Ezekiel is in the inner court now, and the ___ of the LORD fills the temple.

cards.text: The man is still standing right beside Ezekiel, so it's not him talking. Someone is speaking to Ezekiel from INSIDE the temple.

cards.question: From inside the temple, God says, “Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet.” What does He say He will do there?

answers.text: Rule from there for a season
Judge the nations one last time

cards.text: He says Israel and their kings will never again defile His holy name. Back then, they put their threshold right next to His, with only a wall between Him and them.

cards.question: God says that when they built right up against His temple, He overlooked the abominations they committed. True or false?

cards.text: Then God says to let them remove their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings far from Him, and He will dwell among them forever. That promise AGAIN, friend.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to describe the temple to the people of Israel, so that they may be ___ of their iniquities.
If Israel is ashamed of all they've done, God tells Ezekiel to write the temple's design down where they can see it. True or false?
Then God gives Ezekiel the law of the temple. What does it say about all the temple's surrounding territory on top of the mountain?

answers.text: It will belong to the king
It will be open for trade

cards.text: Then God gives the altar's measurements in long cubits: a gutter at the base, ledges stepping up, a square hearth twelve cubits each way with four horns, and steps facing east. Friend, I measure chocolate chips by the mustache-full.

Then the Lord GOD gives the statutes for the altar's first days, served by the Levitical priests from the family of Zadok, a priest in King David's day (2 Samuel 8:17). For seven days come sin offerings and burnt offerings, blood on the altar's horns and salt on the burnt offerings, until the altar is cleansed and consecrated.

cards.question: From the eighth day on, the priests present burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. What does the Lord GOD say then?

answers.text: Then I will send you out

cards.text: The glory fills the temple, and Ezekiel has his instructions. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because trust me, this vision's not done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says a man has been walking Ezekiel around the temple with a measuring rod. That comes from earlier chapters (Ezekiel 40:3 and 40-42), not 43:1. The card gives no reference for it and cites only Ezekiel 43:1.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "asleep" is not the same kind of thing as "facedown" and "backward." Those two are ways of falling. "Asleep" is a state.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The answer is False, but no card ever says what God actually did: "Therefore I have consumed them in My anger" (43:8). The baker leaves knowing only that God did not overlook the abominations, and misses an important detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card blanks a word from God's line in 43:10, and no story card sets it up. Nothing told so far points to "ashamed" over "afraid" or "free," so the baker is guessing the wording of a prophetic line instead of reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to pick God's exact closing words ("Then I will accept you" against "Then I will test you" and "Then I will send you out"). That is guessing the words of a line, not asking about its movement or meaning.

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: The first sentence ("The glory fills the temple, and Ezekiel has his instructions.") recaps earlier cards. It tells nothing from 43:27, the verse the card cites. Since 43:27 is already asked on card 19, this card can be just the story-isn't-over line.
The card cites Ezekiel 43:27, but its recap sentence draws on 43:5 and the passage overall, not on 43:27.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card is a flat restatement of 43:3 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a plain paraphrase of 43:7-8 with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The humor across the walkthrough is mild and sparse. Only cards 1, 3, 7, 13 and 17 carry a joke, and those are gentle asides, not laugh-out-loud moments. Cards 4, 9, 11 and 18 read as neutral narration.

rule.text: **But he is FUNNY.** Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
